_comment: Geometry and archetype definitions for the IOM switchgear SLD generator. All dimensions in drawing units, taken from 8508+A01-000-053/054. 'dx' is measured from the unit power centreline; 'y' is an absolute sheet elevation shared by every unit. Sheet 053 is the datum -- 054 sits about 0.74 lower and is not perfectly parallel, so elevations are read off 053 and 054 is used only for units 053 does not contain.

sheet._pitch_note: Widest cubicle observed in the reference set (unit 8, XFMR feeder). Per IOM practice all units are drawn to the widest unit's width. Reference sheets vary 2.427-3.610 due to hand placement; this generator makes them uniform.
sheet._bus_label_note: Reference sheet 054 omits 'BIL 95kV' and labels its bus 'BUS A' while carrying B-designated units. Generating from one template removes that inconsistency. Moved to 18.433 (was 19.088) in this fork: the bus PT branch now occupies the space directly above bus_y, and at the original position the bus rating text ran straight through the fuse and PT. It is anchored at its top and 1.3 tall, so the band above the branch cannot hold it; placed just below the bus instead, which is clear all the way down to the breaker drawout.
sheet._cubicle_top_note: Raised from 20.602 so bus_y has 5.67 of headroom -- the same the bus-PT-above-breaker branch gets in 8372 unit 6 -- instead of 8508's 2.019, which fits the branch but leaves no room for the unit header. cubicle_bottom and everything below bus_y (breaker, CTs, relay, outgoing) are untouched. Forked from sld_config.json, which keeps its own 20.602 for the 8508 fixtures.

_text_comment: Placements measured from the reference sheets. 'align' is centre (on the unit centreline) or left (offset by dx). The reference uses MTEXT with no wrap width, so lines break only on explicit \P.

cpt_fuse._note: Control power transformer fuse, tapped off the bus to the right.

cpt_fuse_tie_a._note: The tie unit carries two CPT fuses, not one.

relay_box._note: Outline around the protection relay label.

ct_compartment._note: Dashed CT compartment boundary, tall enough for both feeder CTs.

ct_compartment_single._note: Short compartment for a unit carrying one CT (XFMR feeder / riser).

kirk_key_lock._note: Kirk key interlock on the fused disconnect -- a circle centred in a small box.

kirk_key_note.text: @KIRK KEY CAN\P ONLY\PBE REMOVED \PWHEN THE \PDISCONNECT\PIS OPEN.

arrester._note: Self-contained branch: WDDOT tap at (0,0), wire out to HGND2 at +0.677, and a static MTEXT label 'L.A. / 18kV / 15.3kV MCOV'. Because the label is baked in as MTEXT rather than an ATTDEF, the arrester rating is fixed for every unit -- see the 'arrester' column note in units.csv.

ct_protection._note: CTs encircle the conductor -- they do not break the wire run. 'attribs' maps ATTDEF tag -> units.csv column, or a literal when prefixed with @. Roles with no 'attribs' are left blank rather than being filled with the unit tag: in the reference drawings connectors and fuses carry their own ACADE-assigned designations (201PJ121, 201FU72), not the breaker tag.

ct_protection_phase._note: Single-phase mark beside the CT. %%C is AutoCAD's diameter/phase symbol.

ct_horizontal._note: Tie unit only: the outgoing run leaves sideways, so its CT lies on its side and the polarity dot sits beside it rather than above.

feeder_xfmr_leader._note: Leader from the transformer tap out to the continuation note.

pt_relay_box._note: The PT unit's relay sits far lower than a feeder's, level with the metering wiring it watches.

pt_diff_lead._note: Bus-B PT only: the differential CT connection leaves the relay box towards the other bus, which is on another sheet.

ct_tie_upper._note: Third CT, above the tie breaker -- main/tie units only. Its polarity dot sits below it, unlike a feeder CT.

ct_tie_upper_lead._note: Upper CT secondary out to the bus differential relay on the other bus.

tie_outgoing._note: The tie leaves sideways towards the other bus instead of terminating on a connector.

lockout_86_tie._note: The tie's relay box sits above its 86, so the drop runs upward. Unlike the feeder 86, nothing shares this elevation -- every riser stops at the relay box top -- so it keeps the reference offset.

ct_compartment_protection._note: Dashed CT compartment for a lineup with ONE CT set. ct_compartment spans 12.465-9.912 because 8508 units carry two. Extent derived from ct_compartment_single's offsets about its own CT.

ct_ground._note: Motor feeders only. Whether this is a core-balance or a residual connection is still unconfirmed -- the symbol assumes a separate window CT, which is the core-balance case.

bus_pt_data._note: Same geometry as bus_pt, but DESC2 comes from the pt column rather than being fixed at 8508's 7.98KV/120V.

pt_fuse_data._note: Same geometry as pt_fuse, but the rating comes from the pt_secondary_fuse column rather than being fixed at 8508's 6A.

pt_riser_lo._note: Bus up to the PT disconnect -- the tap point off the main bus.

pt_disconnect._note: Drawout disconnect at the base of the PT branch, so the PT can be isolated from the live bus for fuse replacement. The reference uses WD1005 here (8372 sheet 001 y=15.489), but that block is a single polyline that renders as a small marker; VCN1PJ is the drawout symbol this sheet already uses for the breaker contacts, and disc_half_hi/lo above are measured from it via drawout_lower.

pt_riser_mid._note: Disconnect up to the primary fuse.

pt_fuse_pri._note: PT PRIMARY fuse, between the bus and the PT. A primary fault has to open here rather than propagate to the bus, so it cannot sit beyond the PT. Reference: 8372 sheet 001 y=17.566, 'CLF 0.5E'.

pt_riser_hi._note: Primary fuse up to the PT itself -- the fused side of the tap.

bus_pt_above._note: Bus PT on a shunt tap above the bus, fed through the disconnect and primary fuse below it, not in series with the breaker (see 8513 main_pt / 8372 main_with_bus_pt). Scaled 1.4x for legibility.

gen_feeder.description: Generator incoming feeder -- drawout breaker, dual CT, arrester

risers._gap_note: breaks for the CPT fuse body

spurs._note: metering CT secondary, stepping up to the lineup bus at 1.789

customer_feeder.description: Customer feeder -- gen feeder plus control transformer

bess_feeder.description: BESS feeder -- gen feeder plus second fuse

xfmr_feeder.description: Transformer feeder -- fused disconnect with Kirk key, one CT, and the load-side one-line down to the LV panels (reference unit 8)

xfmr_riser.description: Transformer feeder continuation -- same disconnect, Kirk key and CT, but terminating on a connector instead of a transformer (reference unit 14)

pt_riser_tie.description: Bus PT / riser adjacent to a tie -- its relay takes the differential CT from the tie unit (reference unit 9)

control_wiring._joins_note: The PT feeds control power through its power conductor, which lands on the bus rather than ending on a connector -- there is no riser to infer the connection from.

pt_riser.description: Bus PT / riser whose differential CT comes from the other bus, on another sheet (reference unit 11)

main_tie.description: Main / tie breaker -- three CTs, two CPT fuses, breaker stack lowered to clear the upper CT, outgoing run leaving sideways

spurs._note: Mid CT secondary. Unlike a feeder's, this one hops over the CPT riser rather than the riser hopping over it -- that is how the reference draws it.

utility_incoming.description: Utility incomer: cable termination, main breaker, one CT set for protection and metering, three VTs with secondary protection, and the protection relay.

_spec.ct_protection + ct_protection_phase + ct: 'Provide three phase current transformers for protection and metering' -- ONE set, so there is no ct_metering role
_spec.deliberately absent: arrester, lockout_86 and cpt_fuse -- these are 8508 house standard and the specification does not ask for them
_spec.pt_riser_lo + pt_disconnect + pt_riser_m: 'Provide three voltage transformers' and 'Show PT secondary protection'. Drawn as a shunt tap off the bus (series:False + explicit risers), not as part of the breaker's series conductor -- see 8513 main_pt / 8372 main_with_bus_pt for the same pattern in reference-verified drawings. Ordered disconnect -> primary fuse -> PT going up from the bus, measured off issued sheet 8372+A01-050-001.dxf, so the fuse can actually clear a PT primary fault instead of sitting downstream of it.

utility_incoming._open: PT placement follows 8372 sheet 001: tapped off the bus, above it, on the breaker's own centreline, through a disconnect and primary fuse. The specification asks for 'PT secondary protection' but names no primary fuse rating, and the reference's own CLF 0.5E is a 4160V part -- so pt_primary_fuse is currently blank in the CSV and the fuse renders unlabelled. A rating needs picking for 15kV before this sheet is issued. The spec also still does not say whether the incomer's VTs sit in this cubicle or an adjacent one; on 8372 the line PT was housed next door.

motor_feeder.description: Motor feeder: feeder breaker, phase CTs, a separate ground-fault CT, and a motor protection relay.

_spec.source: Single Line Diagram Assignment 6_16.docx, 'Feeder 2 - Motor Feeder'
_spec.ct_ground: 'Ground-fault CT ratio' -- a separate CT, not a second phase set
_spec.ct_compartment: both CTs sit inside the compartment, so the full-height box applies
_spec.deliberately absent: arrester, lockout_86, cpt_fuse and ct_metering -- 8508 house standard, not asked for. Metering CTs are added only when the customer specifies a metering relay.

motor_feeder._open: outgoing.rotation overridden to 180 (matching drawout_lower) so the exit terminal points down toward the destination label rather than sharing drawout_upper's up-pointing rotation; the shared outgoing role used by 8508 archetypes is unaffected.

feeder_breaker.description: Plain feeder: breaker, one CT set, protection relay. No arrester, no lockout, no metering CT.

_spec.source: Single Line Diagram Assignment 6_16.docx, 'Feeder 1 - Transformer Feeder' and 'Feeder 3 - Future Feeder'
_spec.deliberately absent: arrester, lockout_86, cpt_fuse, ct_metering -- 8508 house standard, not asked for
_spec.note: The assignment calls Feeder 1 a transformer feeder, but it is a breaker feeder. It is NOT the existing xfmr_feeder type, which is a fused disconnect with a Kirk key.

feeder_breaker._open: outgoing.rotation overridden to 180 (matching drawout_lower) so the exit terminal points down toward the destination label rather than sharing drawout_upper's up-pointing rotation; the shared outgoing role used by 8508 archetypes is unaffected.

bus_pt_only.description: Bus PT cubicle: three bus-connected VTs with secondary protection, supplying the common voltage reference. No breaker.

_spec.source: Single Line Diagram Assignment 6_16.docx, 'Bus Potential Transformers'
_spec.bus_pt_data: 'Provide one set of three bus-connected potential transformers', ratio and connection from the unit table
_spec.deliberately absent: pt_relay_box and the differential lead -- pt_riser_tie carries those because 8508's PT cubicle sits next to a tie. This lineup has no tie.

bus_pt_only._conductor_bottom_note: Same as pt_riser and pt_riser_tie. Without it the run stops at the fuse's lower gap (16.845) and the PT secondary ends in mid-air 0.255 above the control-power bus it declares it feeds. Only visible on a lineup where that bus exists -- the 4-unit assignment has no second participant, so the bus is dropped and the stub never showed.

control_wiring._bus_dx_note: The PT feeds control power through its own power conductor on the centreline, not through a riser at the feeder offset -- so the bus has to come to 0.0, as it does for pt_riser and pt_riser_tie. At the default 1.431 it overshoots the cubicle centreline and ends on nothing.

bus_pt_only._open: The voltage-reference runs from this PT secondary to each feeder relay are called for by the specification but not yet drawn -- they need a lineup-wide control bus, like the ones in the control section.

control._comment: Lineup-wide horizontal control runs. Each spans only the units carrying a participating role, so a run stops where the archetype changes. start_dx/end_dx are offsets from the first/last participating unit's centreline, and an archetype may override its own meeting point via control_wiring.bus_dx. Note that a unit's CT secondary horizontal is NOT a bus -- it is a per-unit spur that steps up to the metering bus, which is why y=10.059 appears in the archetypes rather than here.

buses.name: diff_ct
buses._note: Bus differential CT run from the tie unit back to the PT unit's relay. Only exists on a lineup containing both.
